text:
Priya N: Drafting the release notes for docs publish (0.9.1). Need: 3 bullets, 2 short SDK examples, 1 public-safe known-issue blurb. Can someone take JS + Python?
Theo M: Ill take JS + the canary note. Keep the example minimal.
Kara B: Ill do Python + the known-issue blurb. We should avoid internal incident IDs.
Theo M: JS snippet draft:
```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY })
const r = await client.generate('Top changes summary', { response_format: 'structured_json' })
console.log(r.structured)
```
Kara B: Python snippet draft:
```py
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
resp = client.generate('Top changes summary', response_format='structured_json')
print(resp.structured)
```
Kara B: Known issue (public-safe): "In rare ingestion workloads using prefix caching with short cache TTLs, duplicate embeddings may appear. Mitigation: increase `prefix_cache_ttl` to >=300s or disable prefix caching for ingestion; contact Redwood Support for help."
Theo M: Behavior change line (one-liner): "Canary fallback policy may prefer cost-compatible variants, which can slightly increase median latency in some configs  see routing docs for tuning."
Priya N: Nice. I'll add these to the relnotes draft and open the PR. Please keep snippets as separate commits for review.
DocsBot: PR opened: https://git.redwood.com/redwood/docs/pull/1267 (automated).
SupportBot: Reminder: do not include internal incident numbers in public docs. Use Support contact instead.
Kara B: All set, pushed commits. Ready for copy review.
Theo M: Quick copy pass done, two tiny punctuation nits pushed as suggestions.
Priya N: Thanks — will merge after approvals and CI. I'll send a short changelog email once merged.
